newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania court adjourns ruling in miner's leader case.
newsitem.headline: Romania court adjourns ruling in miner's leader case.

text.p: A Romanian court on Wednesday delayed a ruling on a prosecution request for an extension of an arrest warrant for miners' leader Miron Cosma, detained in connection with his role in a riot in 1991, court sources said.
Prosecutors at the Bucharest court of appeals had asked for a 30-day extension of Cosma's arrest warrant on the ground that he "could become a public menace" if freed, the sources said.
"Investigations could be hampered with Cosma at large," one prosecutor said.
The court, which last month rejected Cosma's request for bail, decided to postpone the ruling until Friday, the sources said.

Cosma was taken into police custody early in January for investigation on charges arising from a 1991 miners' revolt he led, which toppled Romania's first post-communist government. The charges of "undermining state authority" and breaking firearms rules carry up to 15 years in jail.
A trial date has yet to be set.

Cosma led thousands of coalminers on a three-day rampage to Bucharest in 1991, when government offices were torched and three people were killed during clashes with security forces. The riots led to the ousting of reformist Prime Minister Petre Roman.

Miners from the Jiu Valley coalfield threatened last week to come to Bucharest to stage silent rallies outside the police station where Cosma is detained. Others said they would go on hunger strike in support of their leader.
But Interior Minister Gavril Dejeu took a hard stand on the issue this week, saying the authorities would neither tolerate nor give in to any show of force or pressure from miners.
The new centrist government has pledged to take steps against those responsible for the waves of political violence during 1990 and 1991.
